summary.en: Venture Catalysts (VCats) is a Mumbai-based, angel-led 'integrated incubator' founded in 2016 by Dr. Apoorva Ranjan Sharma and partners. It has backed 500+ startups across 40+ sectors and 650+ districts, combining seed cheques (typically INR 3–15 crore, plus smaller idea-stage cheques via its 9Unicorns/100Unicorns vehicle) with mentorship and access to a 4,500+ investor community. Notable portfolio companies include BharatPe, Beardo and Fynd.

summary.en: GSF, founded in 2011 by Rajesh Sawhney, is one of India's first multi-city tech accelerators / early-stage incubators, backed by leading digital founders and venture funds. It prefers to write the first cheque (~$50K–$200K) and runs a 90-day Founders Academy. Portfolio includes Whatfix, Quizizz, CityMall and Slintel; notable exits include Little Eye Labs (to Facebook), DailyRounds (to M3) and Pokkt (to AnyMind).

summary.en: 91springboard, founded in 2013, is India's largest coworking operator that doubles as a startup hub, community and micro-VC. As an Established Incubation Centre under NITI Aayog's Atal Innovation Mission, it can invest up to Rs 12.5 lakh per startup; it reports having incubated ~150 startups and funded 11, and has invested in companies such as Squad, NeoStencil and LogicRoots.

Shibulal (with Srinath Batni, Tarun Khanna and CEO Ganapathy Venugopal), is a Bengaluru-based early-stage seed fund and accelerator/incubator. summary.en: NASSCOM 10,000 Startups, launched in 2013 by India's tech industry body NASSCOM, is a flagship, equity-free incubation program. It runs co-working 'Startup Warehouses' in cities including Bengaluru, Pune, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai, and provides mentorship, ~$25,000+ in corporate credits, corporate pilots and access to 500+ investors. It reports impacting 11,500+ startups and helping fund 650 over a decade, taking no equity.

verification_notes: NASSCOM 10,000 Startups is run by NASSCOM (a private, non-profit industry association) but is co-funded/supported by state governments and is equity-free — it facilitates rather than directly makes equity investments, so its 'investing' role is indirect. Included because it is a major private-sector incubation hub that supports startups; subtype tags flag the accelerator and public-program dimensions. Metrics (11,500+ impacted / 650 funded) are program-cumulative over ~a decade. HQ city (Noida, NASSCOM HQ) is the parent body location.
